original_text: The 75% Rule for 3-Operand ISAs: across AVX2, AVX-512, and AArch64 NEON, the optimal accumulator count reaches 75% of the architectural register file.
direct_evidence: Synthetic loop unroll on Clang 21.1.8 with -fverbose-asm # Spill comments
indirect_evidence: OpenBLAS 16x6 (12 accs on AVX2) and 8x12 (24 accs on NEON)
missing_evidence: None (repaired regex detector with verified -fverbose-asm stack annotations)
falsification_test: Positive/negative control spill detector on Clang 21.1.8 with varying unroll geometries
independent_check: Manual assembly audit of .LBB0_ loop bodies
acceptance_criteria: Must verify with verbose-asm spill markers; if ratio varies with load/broadcast patterns, downgrade from 'Law' to 'Empirical Heuristic'
observed_result: In 2D microkernels, live loads and broadcasts reduce available accumulator capacity to ~75% of register file; 1D sequential loops sustain higher counts.
contradiction_found: Ratio varies between 1D loops and 2D block microkernels with multiple broadcasts.
final_text: In 2D matrix microkernels, live vector loads and broadcasts reduce usable accumulator capacity to approximately 70-75% of the architectural register file on 3-operand ISAs.

original_text: The 25% Rule for 2-Operand Destructive ISAs: In 2-operand ISAs (SSE4.2), the accumulator budget collapses to 25% of the register file (4 accumulators out of 16).
direct_evidence: SSE4.2 compilation with -fverbose-asm showing 0 spills at 4 accs and 4 spills at 8 accs
falsification_test: Manual assembly audit + verbose-asm spill analysis on SSE4.2 loop
acceptance_criteria: Confirm exact spill point via verbose-asm comments; downgrade from 'Law' to 'Observed Heuristic'
observed_result: Spills begin at 8 accumulators (4 spills) and increase linearly with accumulator count.
contradiction_found: Formulation as universal law overstated what is an observed property of destructive instruction scheduling.
final_text: On 2-operand destructive ISAs (SSE4.2), register spills emerge starting at 8 accumulators, limiting zero-spill accumulator capacity to 4 vectors (25% of the register file).

original_text: Hand-crafting thousands of assembly microkernels is completely unnecessary when structural vector unrolling caps are enforced.
claim_scope: Universal compiler capability replacing hand-written BLAS
direct_evidence: Compiled 16x4 and 16x6 vector contractions on Clang 21.1.8 with 0 inner spills
falsification_test: Lower structured vector contraction to LLVM assembly and compare FMA density, software prefetch instructions, and load interleaving against OpenBLAS Haswell assembly
independent_check: llvm-mca throughput analysis and physical register inspection
acceptance_criteria: Reject 'completely unnecessary'; narrow to 'For tested dense contraction shapes and bounded tile geometries, structured MLIR vectorization generates spill-free FMA loops without hand-written assembly'
observed_result: Dense 16x4 FMA loops compile with 0 inner spills; however, OpenBLAS includes hand-tuned prefetch instructions (prefetcht0 512) and custom stride handling not synthesized by default LLVM lowering.
contradiction_found: Sweeping claim that assembly is 'completely unnecessary' ignores domain-specific prefetching and custom tail masking.
final_text: For tested dense contraction shapes and bounded tile geometries (16x4 on AVX2), structured vector contraction lowering generates spill-free, dual-issue FMA microkernels without handwritten assembly. Specialized optimizations (software prefetching, non-unit stride packing, custom tail masks) remain domain-specific.

original_text: Packing overhead < 2%; 3-5x speedup; N >= 128 large GEMM; N <= 32 small GEMM; generic LLVM 20-40% of peak; OpenBLAS > 90% of peak.
direct_evidence: Theoretical formula R = M / MR and OpenBLAS KERNEL.HASWELL constants
indirect_evidence: OpenBLAS block size constants (GEMM_P=504, GEMM_Q=128, GEMM_R=4096)
falsification_test: Run controlled host benchmark across shape sweep (16, 32, 64, 128, 256) comparing Naive C, Tiled C, and fused paths
negative_control: Skinny matrix (M=1024, N=4, K=1024) where packing is unamortized
independent_check: OpenBLAS source code inspection of dynamic shape dispatch thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Label theoretical formulas as formulas; cite OpenBLAS source constants for library thresholds; replace unmeasured global percentages with host benchmark data
observed_result: Theoretical amortization formula (1/(2N) + 1/(2M)) confirms < 1% overhead for N >= 128 and > 6% overhead for N <= 16. OpenBLAS source confirms GEMM_P=504, GEMM_Q=128, GEMM_R=4096.
contradiction_found: Stating numbers as empirical global constants rather than theoretical bounds and library-specific parameters.
final_scope: Theoretical Amortization Model & Source-Documented Library Constants
final_text: Packing overhead amortizes to < 1% for N >= 128 according to the theoretical model (1/(2N) + 1/(2M)), and OpenBLAS configures cache blocks at GEMM_P=504, GEMM_Q=128, GEMM_R=4096, while bypassing packing for small shapes (N <= 16-32).

original_text: Post-op epilogue fusion 100% eliminates intermediate RAM traffic and delivers up to 2x speedup; classical CBLAS forces RAM round trip.
claim_scope: Hardware memory bus traffic & performance claim
direct_evidence: Logical program dataflow (store C + subsequent load C eliminated)
missing_evidence: Hardware counter validation of physical DRAM bus traffic vs L1/L2/L3 cache residency; measured benchmark on cache-resident vs cache-exceeding matrices
falsification_test: Run host microbenchmark comparing GEMM+ReLU fused vs separate across small (16x16, 32x32), medium (64x64, 128x128), and large (256x256) matrices
negative_control: Small matrix (16x16, 32x32) where entire matrix fits in L1 cache (zero DRAM traffic in both cases)
acceptance_criteria: Replace '100% eliminates RAM traffic' with 'eliminates intermediate store/reload pass at the program level; physical DRAM traffic reduction depends on working-set cache residency'
observed_result: Host benchmark demonstrated that for compute-bound GEMM, arithmetic dominates (>99.5%), producing minimal whole-operation speedup (~0.95-1.0x). Fused post-ops eliminate the logical program store/reload pass, saving DRAM traffic only when matrices exceed CPU cache capacity.
contradiction_found: Claiming 2x speedup on compute-bound GEMM+ReLU was false; 2x speedups occur on memory-bandwidth-bound elementwise chains.
final_text: Post-op epilogue fusion eliminates the intermediate store and reload pass at the program and cache level. Physical DRAM bandwidth savings occur when matrix sizes exceed CPU cache capacity or across elementwise operator chains.

original_text: TTI getRegisterBitWidth, getNumberOfRegisters, getInterleaveCount are 100% stable with exact same signature and semantics across LLVM 20, 21, and 22.
missing_evidence: Direct side-by-side header comparison of declarations, default arguments, return types, and callers across LLVM 20.1.8, 21.1.8, and 22.1.8
falsification_test: Diff TargetTransformInfo.h across all three installed toolchain prefixes C:\Users\hamza\tools\llvm-20.1.8, llvm-21.1.8, llvm-22.1.8
negative_control: Diff LibTooling / AST headers (known to churn)
independent_check: LLVM git commit history between 20.x, 21.x, and 22.x
acceptance_criteria: Verify exact C++ declarations; replace '100% stable' with verified classification ('signature_stable', 'semantic_contract_stable')
observed_result: Header diff verified that getRegisterBitWidth, getNumberOfRegisters, and getMaxInterleaveFactor (corrected method name) maintain identical C++ signatures and semantic contracts across LLVM 20.1.8, 21.1.8, and 22.1.8.
contradiction_found: Initial findings referenced getInterleaveCount (internal helper) instead of the public getMaxInterleaveFactor(ElementCount VF) interface.
final_text: TargetTransformInfo public query methods (getRegisterBitWidth, getNumberOfRegisters, getMaxInterleaveFactor) are signature-stable and semantic-contract-stable across LLVM 20.1.8, 21.1.8, and 22.1.8.

missing_evidence: No AMX tile instructions (tileloadd, tdpbf16ps, tilestored, ldtilecfg) were generated or inspected; ARM SME was not compiled with real SME intrinsics
falsification_test: Author and compile a real AMX intrinsic test generating tileloadd, tdpbf16ps, and tilestored in Clang 21.1.8; probe ARM SME with +sme flags and inspect assembly

original_text: LLVM cannot synthesize data packing automatically.
direct_evidence: Standard LoopVectorize on strided GEMM does not emit packing buffers
indirect_evidence: C standard forbids arbitrary heap allocation without user request
missing_evidence: Distinction between core LLVM LoopVectorize vs Polly polyhedral pass vs MLIR bufferization
falsification_test: Check whether Clang -O3 -mllvm -polly can synthesize packing; check if MLIR linalg.pack pass can synthesize packing
negative_control: Standard Clang -O3 without Polly (does not pack)
acceptance_criteria: Refine 'cannot' to: 'The standard LLVM middle-end loop optimizer does not synthesize global or thread-local memory packing buffers from strided loops by default; packing layout transformations require polyhedral passes, MLIR structured operations (linalg.pack), or explicit runtime workspace management'
observed_result: Standard LoopVectorize operates strictly in-place; MLIR supports explicit linalg.pack operations, and Polly supports polyhedral array packing.
contradiction_found: Broad use of 'cannot' obscured the capability of specialized upstream passes (MLIR linalg.pack, Polly).
final_scope: Standard LLVM Middle-End Default Loop Optimizer Scope
final_text: The standard LLVM middle-end loop optimizer does not synthesize memory packing buffers from strided loops by default. Data packing transformations require structured MLIR operations (linalg.pack), polyhedral optimization (Polly), or caller-managed runtime workspace buffers.
